evals.prompt: I have a recorded customer call saved as call_042.wav and I just want the full transcript as plain text, no streaming. Show me exactly how to call this service's API and what the response looks like.
evals.expected_output: A correct batch transcription walkthrough using the right endpoint, port, and multipart field.
expectations: Uses POST /v1/audio/transcriptions with file as the multipart field.
Uses port 8010 (not 8000 or 8080).
Does not set stream=true since the user wants a single response.
Mentions the X-Session-ID response header.
Shows a curl or client example with file=@call_042.wav.

evals.prompt: I already use the official OpenAI Python SDK in my app for Whisper streaming transcription. I want to point it at this self-hosted service instead and keep getting incremental text as it transcribes. What exactly do I change?
evals.expected_output: A correct OpenAI-SDK-compatible streaming integration using stream=true against this service's base_url.
expectations: Sets base_url to http://127.0.0.1:8010/v1 (or equivalent host) with a placeholder api_key.
Uses model="whisper-1" and stream=True in the SDK call.
Specifies response_format as json or verbose_json, not srt/vtt/text.
Describes handling transcript.text.delta and transcript.text.done events.
Mentions the [DONE] sentinel as the stream terminator.

evals.prompt: My client uploads a subtitle file request with response_format=srt and stream=true and gets an HTTP 400. Why, and what should I change if I still want incremental output?
evals.expected_output: A correct explanation of the stream/response_format constraint and a working alternative.
expectations: States that stream=true requires response_format to be json or verbose_json.
States that srt, vtt, and text return HTTP 400 when combined with stream=true.
Offers switching response_format to json/verbose_json as the fix if streaming is required.
Alternatively offers dropping stream=true if srt output is required.
Does not suggest this is a bug to work around with retries.

evals.prompt: I want to build a live microphone transcription feature in my desktop app using this service. I was assuming I just open a WebSocket and the service listens to my machine's mic directly similar to some other services. Is that right, and how do I actually stream audio to it?
evals.expected_output: A correct explanation that the client owns audio capture, plus the right WebSocket integration shape.
expectations: Corrects the assumption: the service does not capture the microphone itself; the client must capture and stream audio.
Specifies connecting to WS /v1/realtime with intent=transcription.
States the audio must be base64-encoded PCM16, mono.
Describes sending input_audio_buffer.append messages with the audio payload.
Mentions reacting to input_audio_buffer.speech_started/speech_stopped and the transcription delta/completed events.

evals.prompt: I'm streaming audio to /v1/realtime from a quiet lapel mic recording and input_audio_buffer.speech_started never fires, so I never get a transcript. What should I check first?
evals.expected_output: A client-side diagnosis focused on VAD threshold and audio encoding correctness.
expectations: Suggests lowering the VAD threshold via a session.update message for quiet audio.
States the default threshold is normalized RMS (around 0.02), not a neural VAD probability.
Checks that audio is actually PCM16 mono and matches the declared sample rate.
Notes the service does not resample or transcode in the socket layer.
Mentions input_audio_buffer.commit as a way to force a transcript if VAD is the blocker, or disabling VAD entirely with turn_detection: null.

evals.prompt: I want every uploaded chunk of a long file to produce a sentiment label so I can see mood shift over the call, alongside the transcript. How do I get that from this service?
evals.expected_output: An accurate answer about where sentiment appears in responses and that it is a deployment-level setting.
expectations: States that sentiment_summary appears in the transcript.text.done / .completed events or final JSON body only when the deployed service has sentiment enabled.
Clarifies that enabling sentiment is a deployment-time config setting (sentiment.enabled), not a per-request flag the client can set.
Does not claim a request-level parameter can turn sentiment on if it is disabled server-side.
Recommends checking with the deployment owner if sentiment fields are missing.
Avoids conflating sentiment with the (unrelated) diarization feature.

evals.prompt: I set device=GPU as a form field when calling the NDJSON streaming endpoint /v1/audio/transcriptions/stream, but it doesn't seem to change anything. Is this field supported there?
evals.expected_output: A correct explanation of which endpoints support the per-request device override.
expectations: States that the per-request device override only applies to POST /v1/audio/transcriptions (single-response and stream=true forms).
States that /v1/audio/transcriptions/stream always uses the service-configured device and ignores a per-request device field.
Mentions the realtime WebSocket also always uses the service-configured device.
Suggests switching to POST /v1/audio/transcriptions if per-request device selection is required.
Does not claim this is a bug in the NDJSON endpoint.
